--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Span.Defs
theorem coe_sup : ↑(p ⊔ p') = (p + p' : Set M) := by
  ext
  rw [SetLike.mem_coe, mem_sup, Set.mem_add]
  simp

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Pointwise
@[simp]
theorem add_eq_sup (p q : Submodule R M) : p + q = p ⊔ q :=
  rfl

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Span.Defs
theorem mem_sup' : x ∈ p ⊔ p' ↔ ∃ (y : p) (z : p'), (y : M) + z = x :=
  mem_sup.trans <| by simp only [Subtype.exists, exists_prop]

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Span.Defs
theorem span_sup : span R s ⊔ p = span R (s ∪ p) := by rw [Submodule.span_union, p.span_eq]

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Lattice
@[simp]
theorem inf_coe : ↑(p ⊓ q) = (p ∩ q : Set M) :=
  rfl

--src: Mathlib.Order.WithBot
theorem coe_sup [SemilatticeSup α] (a b : α) : ((a ⊔ b : α) : WithBot α) = (a : WithBot α) ⊔ b :=
  rfl

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Defs
@[simp, norm_cast]
theorem coe_add (x y : p) : (↑(x + y) : M) = ↑x + ↑y :=
  rfl

--src: Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Span.Defs
theorem span_eq : span R (p : Set M) = p :=
  span_eq_of_le _ (Subset.refl _) subset_span

--src: Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Defs
protected theorem nonempty : (p : Set M).Nonempty :=
  ⟨0, p.zero_mem⟩

--src: Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Basic
theorem FG.sup {N₁ N₂ : Submodule R M} (hN₁ : N₁.FG) (hN₂ : N₂.FG) : (N₁ ⊔ N₂).FG :=
  let ⟨t₁, ht₁⟩ := fg_def.1 hN₁
  let ⟨t₂, ht₂⟩ := fg_def.1 hN₂
  fg_def.2 ⟨t₁ ∪ t₂, ht₁.1.union ht₂.1, by rw [span_union, ht₁.2, ht₂.2]⟩

C1_dependencies.name: Set
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.
-/
def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop
